packageRules.description: The Sigma toolchain (detections/requirements.txt + docker/validation/zircolite-constraints.txt) moves as ONE PR: pySigma, pyparsing and the backends are coupled, so per-package PRs would each go red waiting for the others. Every bump runs the corpus through the hard gates; a red one is the intended conversation, so it is never automerged (#322).

pysigma-backend-sqlite 2.1.0 is the backend's pySigma-2 release (pysigma>=2). Offered alone it is unresolvable against the pinned pysigma 1.5.1, and the host-plane gate goes red at pip install with 0 rows run (#354). Part of the pySigma-1 hold below: DELETE it with the others in the PR that takes pysigma 2.

pySigma-1 hold. pysigma-backend-elasticsearch (2.1.1) and pysigma-backend-kusto (1.0.1) have no pySigma-2 release yet: both declare pysigma<2.0.0, so the grouped bump to pysigma 2 (#353) fails at pip install with ResolutionImpossible and runs nothing. Hold pysigma on 1.x until both backends ship a release that accepts pysigma 2. Then DELETE this rule and the three beside it (sigma-cli, pysigma-backend-splunk, pysigma-backend-sqlite) in the same PR that takes pysigma 2, so the toolchain still moves as one.
Part of the pySigma-1 hold above: sigma-cli 4.0.0 is its first release requiring pysigma>=2.0.0, so it cannot move while pysigma is held. DELETE with the pysigma rule.
Part of the pySigma-1 hold above: pysigma-backend-splunk 3.0.0 is its first release requiring pysigma>=2.0.1, so it cannot move while pysigma is held. DELETE with the pysigma rule.
